Article Title: China hits $1 trillion trade surplus milestone for second year in a row
Article Text:
Representative image

AI demand supports exports, but trade tensions persist

Weak domestic demand adds to export dependence

Oil imports fall despite supply concerns

China's trade surplus crossed $1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year, as strong global demand for high-tech products, fuelled by the race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, helped offset weak domestic consumption.The surplus reached $1.04 trillion between January and October, according to customs data released on Tuesday.China has now recorded a trade surplus of more than $1 trillion for a second consecutive year, reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase but higher than the 33.5% growth forecast by economists in a Reuters poll.Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%.Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October from $133.5 billion in September.The export performance reflects China's growing reliance on overseas demand as subdued domestic consumption and a prolonged property market downturn weigh on its economy.The global AI investment boom has supported sales of Chinese technology products, including semiconductors and electronics, but the expanding surplus is also raising concerns among trading partners.Much of China's export growth this year has been driven by the global push to expand AI infrastructure. Analysts expect demand for Chinese technology products to remain strong into 2027, although the outlook will depend on how long the investment boom lasts.“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote, adding that exports could accelerate further in the fourth quarter before beginning to slow from the first quarter of 2027.Dave Chia, an economist at Moody's Analytics, also expects Chinese exports to remain strong through the rest of the year, led by electronics and automobiles.However, the expanding surplus could intensify trade tensions, particularly with the European Union.European leaders have called for further trade restrictions on China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc over the next few years.Since the measures have yet to take effect, manufacturers are expected to bring forward shipments, supporting exports in the near term.“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.The US-China trade relationship also remains uncertain. Beijing on Monday officially announced a two-month extension of its trade truce with Washington, which was due to expire on November 10.However, China said last week that any expansion of its purchases of US agricultural goods would depend on the implementation of the agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.China's trade surplus with the US narrowed slightly to $32.71 billion in October from $34.01 billion in September, but the gap remains a point of friction between the two economies.Trade is expected to feature prominently in the planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen later this month.The two leaders are expected to meet for the third time this year.The strong export performance comes against the backdrop of subdued consumer spending in China. A prolonged downturn in the property market has weakened household wealth and confidence, leaving domestic demand under pressure.The weakness has also pushed Chinese manufacturers to look overseas for customers. Automobile exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded their 12th consecutive monthly decline, according to separate industry data.AP cited analysts who said overcapacity in several industries, excess domestic savings and weak domestic demand were pushing Chinese companies to sell more goods abroad. Alicia García-Herrero, chief economist for Asia Pacific at Natixis, said the situation was not sustainable.Businesses are also facing intense competition at home. Cinders Zhou, who sells eyewear for a manufacturer in the eastern Chinese city of Linhai, told AP that competition had increasingly centred on price as products across the industry became more similar.“It comes down to product quality, or rather the increasingly the lack of it across the industry, since there's significant homogenization,” Zhou said. “That has forced everyone to compete on price.”Greater dependence on overseas markets also leaves China's economy more exposed to a slowdown in global demand or further trade restrictions. Analysts have warned that any correction in the AI industry could hurt exports of chips and electronics.“If the AI boom slows or turns into a correction, lower chip and electronics prices and smaller shipping volumes would hit China's exports hard,” Chia said, according to AP.China's oil imports fell 13.3% in October compared with a year earlier, although shipments reached their highest level since March as buyers sought supplies following disruptions to Middle East flows caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.The trade figures come ahead of the APEC summit, where trade policy and tariffs are expected to be among the key issues in discussions between Trump and Xi. The two sides had previously proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts following their September summit in Washington, including around $17 billion worth of US agricultural goods.While Chinese officials have maintained that Beijing is not seeking to expand its trade surplus and wants more balanced global trade, the latest figures underline the importance of overseas demand to the country's export-led growth.
Article Summary: Exports rose 35.2% in October from a year earlier in US dollar terms, slightly below September's 36.3% increase. Imports grew 41.6%, accelerating from 31% in September and beating the poll's median forecast of 32%. Despite the stronger import growth, China's trade surplus narrowed to $105.3 billion in October.

Article Title: Russia-US diesel deal delivers results? Lavrov claims prices have already fallen
Article Text:
Russia hails diesel deal with US (representative image)

US-bound shipments face uncertainty

Lavrov raises Ukraine strikes on Russian energy infrastructure

Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov has said an agreement allowing Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets is already being implemented and has helped bring prices down.In an article published in Moscow daily Kommersant on Tuesday, Lavrov said the arrangement was an important contribution to energy security. He also argued that Russia did not use its economy to score political points against countries it considered adversaries or competitors.Also Read| Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey “Since 2022, we have supplied Europe with energy resources worth $320 billion,” Lavrov wrote.“An important contribution to energy security was the agreement between the Russian and US leaders to suspend restrictions on the export of Russian diesel. We have already started implementing it, which immediately brought prices down.”US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. Under the arrangement, Russia agreed to make 300,000 metric tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, of diesel available immediately to the US and global markets, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.The Trump administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the exports.The move came as the US president sought to bring down fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which his Republican Party lost.Lavrov did not provide figures to support his claim that the agreement had lowered diesel prices.US diesel futures have fallen about 11% since the deal was announced, according to Reuters.However, diesel prices at US pumps were at a record high last week when Americans voted, according to price tracker GasBuddy.The arrangement has also faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.Two sanctioned tankers that had initially declared destinations on the US East Coast changed course, while a third vessel travelling across the North Atlantic changed its destination from New York to “for orders”, according to news agency AP.The report said the proposed imports had yet to result in a confirmed US delivery. Analysts also questioned whether the shipments would reach American ports, citing regulatory and sanctions-related concerns.New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill had advised port and terminal operators in the state to reject Russian fuel shipments, warning of possible legal consequences. A bipartisan group of US senators also urged Trump to abandon the arrangement, arguing that it could provide financial support to Moscow.The US Treasury Department, however, maintained that its temporary authorisation for Russian diesel transactions was consistent with previous actions and “in compliance with all applicable laws”.The exemption was issued for the sale, delivery, unloading and import of Russian diesel until April 7.Separately, Russian deputy foreign minister Alexander Pankin said on Monday that the diesel arrangement could provide an opportunity for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between Moscow and Washington.He told the TASS state news agency that the deal could “serve as a foundation for the gradual restoration of business and other ties between our countries”.In his Kommersant article, Lavrov said Russia was working to stabilise global energy markets and ensure energy security, as well as the balanced and sustainable development of countries and regions.He also accused Ukraine of ignoring Trump's calls to stop attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week that Kyiv's forces were continuing their strikes.Russian media have reported that fuel shortages have returned in at least half a dozen Russian regions following Ukrainian attacks on at least eight major oil refineries over the past two weeks.
Article Summary: Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov hails diesel deal with US. Deal allows Russia to resume diesel exports to the United States and global markets. US President Donald Trump announced the deal on October 9. The arrangement has faced uncertainty over whether Russian fuel would reach the US.

Article Title: Oil prices fall over 1% as hopes of Iran, Russia-Ukraine peace talks weigh on market
Article Text:
Brent crude futures declined $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel

Oil prices fell more than 1% on Thursday as investors weighed the possibility of progress in diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict, easing some concerns over potential supply disruptions.Brent crude futures declined $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel by 0141 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped $1.04, or 1.2%, to $85.49. The losses came a day after both benchmarks recovered from two-month lows, with Brent gaining 1.4% and WTI rising 0.6% on Wednesday.Hopes of a breakthrough in the Russia-Ukraine conflict have offered some relief to oil markets. Negotiators from Moscow and Kyiv agreed to a major prisoner exchange following two days of US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi, which concluded on Wednesday. However, disagreements over key issues, particularly territorial control, remain unresolved. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said Kyiv hopes to make tangible progress towards ending the war this year.The possibility of the Iran conflict avoiding further escalation ahead of next week's US-China summit has also influenced market sentiment."Markets are falling on expectations that behind-the-scenes efforts are underway to secure a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine and that it is unlikely the Iran war will escalate ahead of the US-China summit next week," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities.He said the situation around the Strait of Hormuz could nevertheless prevent a steep decline in crude prices."However, given the uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, the markets are unlikely to suffer a significant collapse," Kikukawa said.Tensions over Iran's nuclear programme continue to complicate the prospect of negotiations. Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country and warned of consequences if the US launched fresh strikes. Washington has insisted that nuclear issues must feature in initial negotiations aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, although US officials have played down the need for further military action.On the supply front, OPEC+ crude production recorded a sharp increase in October, driven largely by higher output from Saudi Arabia, even as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz continued to face disruption.US inventory data also pointed to an increase in available supplies. Crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels in the latest week, according to figures from the American Petroleum Institute cited by market sources. The official report from the US Energy Information Administration is due on Thursday, after its release was pushed back by a day because of the Veterans Day holiday.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures declined $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel by 0141 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures dropped $ 1.04, or1.2, to $85.49. Losses came a day after both benchmarks recovered from two-month lows.

Article Title: RBI plans to ban private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in multiple NBFCs: What will change?
Article Text:
RBI plans to tighten rules for PE firms holding stakes in multiple NBFCs

What is controlling stake

Foreign investors step up investments in NBFCs

Industry seeks greater flexibility in ownership rules

NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India ( RBI ) is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking financial company (NBFC).The proposed rules will also distinguish between controlling stakes and smaller financial investments, allowing holdings of 15% or less to attract fewer regulatory checks, sources told Reuters.The move follows the central bank's concerns that financial stress at a global private equity firm or its affiliates could spread across several NBFCs in which it has significant investments.However, the RBI also wants to encourage smaller financial investments that would be subject to less scrutiny, the people said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are private.Currently, a 25% stake in a listed company is considered a controlling stake. However, an investor can also be considered to have control with a smaller shareholding if it can appoint most of the company's directors or influence its management or policy decisions.Investments of 15% or less will be treated as financial investments and face fewer regulatory checks, one of the people said.The RBI will finalise a draft of the proposed rules after seeking public feedback. The rules could be formally issued early next year, the person added.Foreign investors have been showing growing interest in Indian banks and NBFCs, supported by strong demand for credit and low loan delinquencies.Private equity investments in India's financial sector reached around $5.4 billion last year, up 6% from 2024 and 17% from 2023, according to Grant Thornton data. A further $3.6 billion flowed into the sector between January and the end of September this year.The RBI has previously taken steps to prevent investors from holding controlling stakes in multiple NBFCs.Last year, the central bank approved US private equity firm Bain Capital's acquisition of a 41.7% stake in Manappuram Finance on the condition that it sell its 93% holding in another NBFC, Tyger Capital, formerly known as Adani Capital.The same approach has also applied to investors outside the private equity industry.Japan's Mizuho Financial Group holds majority stakes in two NBFCs, Mizuho Capsave and Credit Saison India. It has also announced plans to acquire KKR-backed financial services firm Avendus.The apex bank has asked Mizuho to submit a detailed plan to integrate or consolidate its existing non-bank financial businesses in India. Mizuho Securities did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.The Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association has approached the RBI, seeking permission for different entities within the same group to hold stakes of more than 20% in multiple NBFCs.Siddarth M Pai, co-chair of the association's regulatory affairs committee and founder of venture capital firm 3one4 Capital, said many private equity firms and venture capital funds wanted to invest in fintech and financial services businesses through their different funds. However, ownership limits were making it difficult for them to do so.The sector has also seen two major private equity deals this week. Blackstone agreed to buy a 16% stake in IIFL Finance for $535 million, while Singapore's Temasek will invest around $265 million in Godrej Capital.
Article Summary: The Reserve Bank of India ( RBI ) is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking financial company (NBFC) The proposed rules will also distinguish between controlling stakes and smaller financial investments. The move follows the central bank's concerns that financial stress at a global private equity firm or its affiliates could spread across several NBFCs.

Article Title: Why Anthropic's IPO could follow the SpaceX playbook, and what it means for investors
Article Text:
Anthropic IPO next week

How index inclusion drives demand

What could be different this time?

When AI company Anthropic begins trading after its expected IPO next week, its share price in the initial weeks may depend as much on who is required to buy the stock as on who wants to own it.Investors are looking to Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June, for clues. Its listing changed the playbook for mega-IPOs by triggering rapid inclusion in major stock market indexes, creating a large pool of buyers soon after trading began.Anthropic is expected to follow a similar path. The Claude chatbot maker aims to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares at $70-$78 apiece, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion.Index providers track groups of stocks representing a particular market. Funds that follow these indexes, known as passive funds, must buy shares of companies added to their benchmarks to match the index.Earlier, major providers generally waited weeks or months after an IPO before including a company. But following SpaceX's listing, the rules changed, allowing large companies to enter key indexes much sooner.Anthropic is expected to join at least six major indexes, including FTSE's USA index, the S&P Total Market Index and the Nasdaq 100, within five to 15 days of listing. "Anthropic is a mirror image of the SpaceX IPO. In that regard, it has the same index-related drivers over the first 15 days of trading," said Carsten Hesse, head of index events at Berenberg, as quoted by Reuters.Index analytics firm Intropic estimates that demand from passive funds could account for around 28% of Anthropic's shares on offer, or roughly $19 billion.Funds tracking an index typically buy shares when the inclusion takes effect. But hedge funds and specialist traders often buy earlier, anticipating this demand and hoping to profit from a rise in the share price.The relatively small public float could amplify this effect. Only around 6% of Anthropic's outstanding shares are being offered in the IPO.SpaceX followed a similar pattern. It reserved a fifth of its $75 billion offering for retail investors, more than twice the usual allocation. Retail investors and index funds bought nearly half the shares sold, while other fund managers positioned themselves for further demand.SpaceX shares rose 50% from their opening-day debut price by the third day of trading and remained above the IPO price for the first 15 days. "You don't wait till day 5, day 10, day 15, when you see the implementation of the index upgrades or inclusions," Hesse said. "As we've seen with SpaceX, people are buying early."The start of options trading can also add to early buying. When traders take positions in stock options, they may buy or sell the underlying shares to hedge their exposure. SpaceX and South Korean firm SK Hynix both saw sharp gains on the third day of trading, when options trading began.Anthropic's trajectory could differ, however. Employees, who own around 15 per cent of its equity, will be allowed to sell some shares on the first day. The company is also raising $26 billion through a separate private sale involving investors such as Google, Nvidia and AMD. Those shares will not have a lock-up period, which normally restricts early investors from selling for a specified time.The faster index inclusion of mega-IPOs has created bigger opportunities for funds that trade around index changes. Such investors buy shares ahead of passive funds, hoping to benefit when the latter enter the market.Earlier, these trades were limited by smaller IPO sizes and the risk of too many investors chasing the same opportunity. Mega-listings offer a much larger pool of shares and potential demand. "It's a bit of an evolution of the market," said Brian Hartigan, global head of ETFs and index investments at Invesco."If you're in index rebalancing, these are probably the events of a lifetime," said Bill Park, CIO of Altisma Capital Management.
Article Summary: Anthropic IPO next week expected to trigger rapid inclusion in major stock market indexes. The chatbot maker aims to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares at $70-$78 apiece. Investors are looking to Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June, for clues.

Article Title: As gold falls from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, Indians buy 30% more, spending Rs 72,000 crore on 52 tonnes; silver demand rises 10%
Article Text:
In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%.

Gold price correction from Rs 1.8 lakh peak

Gold generates big returns

Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.The industry body estimated that consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.The increase followed a correction in gold prices from a peak of around Rs 1.8 lakh to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, drawing buyers back into the market. Purchases made in advance of the wedding season, which starts in mid-November and runs until March, also helped boost demand.“Jewellers have made good business in this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali,” IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET.Mehta said the market was witnessing pent-up demand, as several consumers had put off buying gold after Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people not to purchase the metal.“Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing .”The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses.“This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment,” said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council.In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%. The fall was attributed to higher prices, an increase in import duty and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to consumers to refrain from buying gold.Despite the volatility, gold has generated significant returns over the past few years. Prices, which were around Rs 60,000 per 10 grams in 2023, climbed to Rs 80,000 in 2024 and reached Rs 1.15 lakh-Rs 1.20 lakh in 2025. During this year’s Dhanteras-Diwali period, prices stood at approximately Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver has also recorded a substantial appreciation in value.An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers found that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third-highest in a decade, even though prices were around 10% above their level a year earlier.“The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period,” said C Vinod Hayagriv, director of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers.Natural diamonds also held up well, registering their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer recorded a 250% increase in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras, while sales during the Diwali season rose 47%.The performance comes at a time when the natural diamond industry is facing disruption from global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and increasing competition from lab-grown alternatives. However, lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional product category rather than displacing natural diamonds.
Article Summary: Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10%. Trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season. Consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.

Article Title: India’s crude oil imports from Russia hit record high in October; Jamnagar refinery biggest importer
Article Text:
India's imports of Russian crude oil rose in October 2026, up 10% month-on-month.

India’s record purchases from Russia

Who bought Russia’s fossil fuels in October 2026?

Countries imposing sanctions continue to import

India's imports of Russian fossil fuels climbed to a record EUR 6.4 billion in October, fuelled by a steep rise in crude oil purchases, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).The increase has helped Russia record its highest monthly revenue from fossil fuel exports since December 2022, despite Western sanctions.China continued to lead the list of buyers worldwide. It accounted for 51% of Russia's export revenue from the five largest importing countries, with purchases worth EUR 10.7 billion.Also Read | Diversifying away from Russia: Trump admin wants to sell Venezuela oil to India, but how much can it buy? The think tank noted that China and India, Russia's two biggest fossil fuel customers, both recorded their highest monthly purchases since January 2022. The figures underline Moscow's continued reliance on Asian markets, even as Western governments step up restrictions on its energy trade.China bought Russian fossil fuels worth EUR 10.7 billion during October, while India's purchases totalled EUR 6.4 billion. The European Union followed with imports worth EUR 2.2 billion. Turkiye ranked fourth, purchasing EUR 1.1 billion, while South Korea was fifth with imports of EUR 488 million."India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October 2026, importing a total of EUR 6.4 billion of Russian hydrocarbons, its highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022. Crude oil constituted 91 per cent of India's purchases, totalling EUR 5.8 billion. Coal (EUR 333 million) and oil products (EUR 232 million) constituted the remainder of its monthly Russian imports," the report said."India's imports of Russian crude oil rose in October 2026, up 10% month-on-month. Russian crude imports rose at all three of India's largest importing refineries: (Nayara Energy's) Vadinar (up 12 per cent month-on-month), ( Reliance Industries Ltd's) Jamnagar (up 22 per cent), and (Indian Oil Corporation Ltd's) Paradip (up 28 per cent)," CREA said."This increase has once again made the Jamnagar refinery the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude."The European Union ranked third among Russia's biggest fossil fuel buyers in October 2026. Its purchases accounted for 11 per cent of the export revenues generated by the top five importing countries, which was around EUR 2.2 billion.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei processing Russian crude also shipped oil products worth EUR 1.6 billion to countries that had imposed sanctions on Russia following its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022."The destinations include the EU (EUR 1.2 billion), Australia (EUR 271 million), the US (EUR 94 million), and New Zealand (EUR 23 million). An estimated EUR 389 million of these products were refined from Russian crude."CREA said Russia's earnings from fossil fuel exports rose 14 per cent month-on-month in October to EUR 754 million a day, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Higher crude oil prices and record revenues from seaborne oil shipments helped counter the impact of Western sanctions, allowing Moscow to maintain its energy exports.Russia's export earnings increased even though its overall fossil fuel export volumes remained largely stable, indicating that higher international energy prices played a growing role in boosting its revenues. The rise also came amid elevated global oil and gas prices linked to the conflict in the Middle East and disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Exports travelling to the US in October came from India’s Jamnagar refinery (EUR 94 mn). Between August and October 2026, 30% of the Jamnagar refinery’s crude imports came from Russia.CREA estimated that the rise in oil and gas prices following the US-Israel strikes on Iran added $35.9 billion, or approximately EUR 31 billion, to Russia's seaborne fossil fuel export revenues over the following six months.
Article Summary: China bought Russian fossil fuels worth EUR 10.7 billion during October, while India's purchases totalled EUR 6.4 billion. Russia's earnings from fossil fuel exports rose 14 per cent month-on-month in October to EUR 754 million a day, the highest monthly level since December 2022.

Article Title: Kia to invest $2 billion in new Andhra plant, boost annual car production capacity to 6.3 lakh
Article Text:
Kia plans second Andhra Pradesh plant with $2 billion investment

Kia looks to ramp up production capacity to 6.3 lakh

From electric to CNG: Kia plans launches across segments

NEW DELHI: Kia India giving a major boost to its Andhra Pradesh manufacturing operations, with a $2 billion investment in a new plant. The proposed facility is expected to create around 12,000 jobs and take the South Korean automaker's annual production capacity to 6.3 lakh vehicles.Kia India managing director and CEO Gwanggu Lee announced the expansion while speaking at the CII Partnership Summit on Thursday. "I am so delighted to announce the expansion of Kia's presence in Andhra Pradesh through the establishment of an additional manufacturing plant," he said.However, the company has not specified when it plans to make the investment or when the additional production capacity will become operational.Kia India currently has a manufacturing plant in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, which was set up in 2017. The facility has an annual production capacity of 4.30 lakh vehicles. The proposed new plant will increase the company's total annual capacity to 6.30 lakh units.In financial year 2026, Kia India produced 3.17 lakh vehicles. Of these, 2.89 lakh units were dispatched in the domestic market, while 27,953 units were exported.Speaking about the company's growth in India, Lee said its first manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh was set up and commissioned in a record 14 months."Our journey in Andhra Pradesh began in 2017, when our first manufacturing plant was established and commissioned in a record time of just 14 months. Kia is proud of being among India's leading automotive manufacturers and the fastest OEM to achieve one million vehicle production in just four years and two million vehicles within seven years, Lee said.The manufacturing expansion comes as Kia prepares to introduce several models across different powertrains to increase its share in India's passenger vehicle market.Apart from its battery-electric, petrol and diesel vehicles, the automaker is also planning to launch hybrid models. It has already announced its entry into the CNG segment with the Carens.Kia recently launched a facelifted version of its popular Seltos mid-size SUV and the new Sorento. The company expects both models to generate strong volumes going forward.The Korean giant's existing India portfolio also includes the Sonet, Syros, Carens and Carnival SUVs.Kia's manufacturing facility in Anantapur has also grown into an important export hub. The plant has exported more than 4.1 lakh vehicles and kits to nearly 100 countries.Lee said the facility's export operations have strengthened India's position as a global manufacturing powerhouse and supported the vision of Make it India for the world.
Article Summary: Kia India plans second Andhra Pradesh plant with $2 billion investment. The proposed facility is expected to create around 12,000 jobs. Kia India currently has a manufacturing plant in Anantapur. The facility has an annual production capacity of 4.30 lakh vehicles.

Article Title: Noel Tata passes baton to Bahram Vakil at Tata Investment Corporation
Article Text:
Noel Tata passes baton to Bahram Vakil

MUMBAI: Tata Investment Corporation has appointed Bahram Vakil as chairman, completing a boardroom handover that has seen Noel Tata step down from a string of Tata companies on reaching the group’s retirement age.The appointment is the second in quick succession for Vakil. He had already been named chairman of Trent, the group’s retail arm behind Westside and Zudio, on the same timetable, succeeding Noel.The reshuffle extends beyond Tata Investment and Trent. At Tata International, T V Narendran, chief executive and managing director of Tata Steel, will become chairman, succeeding Noel Tata. Narendran, already a non-executive director on the Tata International board, takes over as part of the same retirement-driven change.Vakil, co-founder of law firm AZB & Partners, takes over from Nov 12, a day after Noel Tata retired as chairman and director at the close of business on November 11. Noel, who joined the board in June 2004 and had chaired the company since June 2010, becomes chairman emeritus.For a group long defined by family stewardship and Tata lifers, the appointment is notable. Vakil is a corporate lawyer, not an operating executive.He is, however, no stranger to the group. He became vice-chairman and independent director of Tata Investment in March 2025, giving him a front-row seat before his elevation.There is also precedent for turning to an outsider. In 2005, Ratan Tata stepped down as chairman of VSNL, now Tata Communications and independent director Subodh Bhargava took over. In 2017, private equity veteran Renuka Ramnath became chairperson of Tata Communications, succeeding Bhargava.Under Tata Group guidelines, non-executive, non-independent directors retire at 70. Noel turns 70 on Nov 12. He will remain chairman of Tata Trusts and a Tata Trusts nominee on the board of Tata Sons, the holding company. Narendran's appointment keeps Tata International, the group’s trading and distribution arm, under a Tata operating chief, in contrast to Tata Investment and Trent, where the chairmanship has passed to an outside professional. At Voltas, Sunil D’Souza, chief executive of Tata Consumer Products, has also taken over as chairman.
Article Summary: Noel Tata steps down from a string of Tata companies on reaching the group’s retirement age. The appointment is the second in quick succession for Vakil. The reshuffle extends beyond Tata Investment and Trent. At Tata International, T V Narendran will become chairman, succeeding Noel Tata.

Article Title: India back among world’s top 5 biggest stock markets with record rally; value climbs to $5.4 trillion
Article Text:
Foreign investors have returned to Indian equities as net buyers in November.

India back in top 5 league

India has reclaimed its position as the world’s fifth largest stock market by value, courtesy the record rally its indices have seen in the last ten trading sessions.Indian equities have gained around $640 billion in market value since late October, benefiting from weakening investor enthusiasm for AI-related stocks and a steep fall in oil prices.Bank of America has raised its estimate for India’s economic growth in the third quarter of 2026 to 7.7% year-on-year, compared with its earlier projection of 7.2%, a report published earlier this week showed.Moody’s too has lifted the growth forecast from 6.5% to 7%. Global brokerages have upgraded their outlook for the stock market.Also Read | Sensex erases US-Iran war losses, rises nearly 12% in just 10 sessions: What should your investment strategy be? The rally has lifted the market’s total value to approximately $5.4 trillion, allowing India to overtake Taiwan and reclaim its position as the world’s fifth-largest stock market, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.The shift in global investment flows has also set India apart from other markets. While overseas investors are returning to Indian equities, Taiwan recorded its highest-ever foreign fund outflows in October as AI-linked stocks came under a worldwide selloff.The developments prompted authorities there to introduce measures to support the market. South Korea, another major beneficiary of investor interest in technology stocks, has meanwhile dropped to ninth place, slipping behind Canada and the UK. Sensex climbed 772 points to reach its highest level in nearly nine months and the Nifty ending above 25,250 on Wednesday. Buying by foreign investors, corporate earnings for the July-September quarter that exceeded expectations, and a continued easing in crude oil prices are supporting the rally.Foreign investors have returned to Indian equities as net buyers in November. This follows two consecutive months of net outflows. The reversal has been supported by a sell-off in global markets linked to artificial intelligence investments, robust domestic earnings growth and attractive valuations among large-cap stocks.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that the Nifty rally of 9.55% in seven trading sessions so far in November is being led primarily by the aggressive buying by the FIIs.“The tug of war between the FIIs and DIIs till November saw the FIIs on the sell side and DIIs on the buy side. This trend is likely to continue and has the potential to reach an all-time high number,” he says.“Impressive earnings growth as evidenced by the good Q2 results and the macro relief from lower crude prices (Brent around $92) will support the rally. Article Title: Son faced tax notices over Rs 20.23 lakh property purchase and Rs 13.04 lakh cash deposits; ITAT accepts mother's gold-sale gift deed evidence and deletes addition
Article Text:
The person’s counsel told ITAT Jaipur the assessee's mother had sold her old gold jewellery and given her son Rs 16 lakh in cash. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT rule in favour of the assessee?

You buy a property and also deposit cash in your bank account. The Income Tax department treats both as unexplained income and asks you to file your income tax return. What do you do?A resident of Jaipur attracted the Income Tax Department's attention after purchasing a property and depositing cash in his bank account without filing an income tax return.A man purchased a property worth Rs 20.23 lakh and deposited Rs 13.04 lakh in cash into his bank account. The department had received information about these transactions and began proceedings to investigate the source of the funds used for the investment and cash deposits.During the proceedings, the taxpayer filed his income tax return, declaring an income of Rs 2,14,997. However, the Assessing Officer (AO) treated both the property investment of Rs 20,23,778 and the cash deposits of Rs 13,04,900 as unexplained. This resulted in additions of Rs 33,28,678, or approximately Rs 33.29 lakh, to the man’s income.The person contested the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals). The appellate authority removed the addition relating to the property purchase but retained the Rs 13,04,900 addition for unexplained cash deposits.He subsequently approached the Jaipur Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), challenging the amount that continued to be treated as unexplained income.In an order dated October 6, 2026, ITAT Jaipur decided the matter in the man’s favour and deleted the addition of Rs 13,04,900 relating to the cash deposits. The addition concerning the property investment had already been removed by the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).The person’s counsel told ITAT Jaipur the assessee’s mother had sold her old gold jewellery and given her son Rs 16 lakh in cash. A registered valuer had assessed the jewellery's value at Rs 18,36,230 in 2011.The Assessing Officer was not satisfied with this explanation because the documents relating to the jewellery sale did not list the individual gold items. The cousel countered that old jewellery is commonly sold in the trade on the basis of its aggregate weight, without each item being separately described on the invoice.The AO had also raised questions about the difference between the total weight recorded in the valuation report and the quantity of jewellery sold. Responding to this objection, the counsel submitted that the person’s mother had sold 642.300 grams of jewellery for Rs 16,10,567 and subsequently gifted Rs 16 lakh to her son.To support the explanation, the person relied on a notarised gift deed bearing the signatures of two witnesses and the valuation report prepared by the registered valuer. The tribunal also noted that the man had deposited a total of Rs 16,05,000 into his bank account between February 4 and March 31, 2012.After examining the arguments and supporting documents, ITAT Jaipur accepted the man’s explanation for the source of the cash deposits.The tribunal observed: “This gift is from the mother only which is within the relatives as defined in Section 2(41). Further the assesee’s mother in her old age gifted part of the amount from sale of her gold jewellery given as gift to the assessee, which cannot be doubted, since the same is supported by valid notarised Gift Deed with two witnesses and value of the jewels were determined by Registered Valuer. Thus the addition made by the AO is liable to be deleted. ”On this basis, the tribunal removed the addition of Rs 13,04,900 that had been made for unexplained cash deposits.Chartered Accountant Varun Singhal told ET that taxpayers seeking to explain the source of funds through a gift should take certain precautions. They should establish where the donor obtained the money instead of relying only on documentation confirming that the gift was made. It is also important to retain documents created at the relevant time, such as the gift deed, valuation report and jewellery-sale invoice.Taxpayers should maintain a clear documentary trail connecting the gift to the subsequent bank deposits, ensuring that the dates and amounts can be matched. Where available, the donor's bank statements and other financial records should also be preserved.
Article Summary: A man purchased a property worth Rs 20.23 lakh and deposited Rs 13.04 lakh in cash into his bank account. The Income Tax department treats both as unexplained income and asks you to file your income tax return. The person contested the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) The appellate authority removed the addition relating to the property purchase but retained the Rs 13,04,900 addition for unexplained cash deposits.

Article Title: Qualcomm layoffs 1,500 employees in India amid restructuring
Article Text:
Revoked Slack, 4-6am emails: Oracle’s second layoff round hits India

Bengaluru: Qualcomm has begun a round of layoffs in India, affecting around 1,500 employees, amid a renewed emphasis on performance and organisational efficiency by its chief executive Cristiano Amon.The job cuts come even as the US semiconductor highlighted India’s growing importance in its global engineering and semiconductor development operations. The company has around 18,000 employees in India. An email sent to Qualcomm on the layoffs in India didn’t elicit a response till press time.In February, Qualcomm Technologies announced the successful tape-out of its 2nm semiconductor design, a significant milestone in advanced chip design that underscored the capabilities of its engineering teams in India. The work involved collaboration across its engineering development centres in Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad.The Bengaluru campus is a key engineering hub for the development of next-generation wireless, AI, computing and system-level technologies.These centres constitute one of Qualcomm’s most advanced engineering footprints globally and its largest engineering workforce outside the US.Its Indian teams contribute to design implementation, validation, AI optimisation and system integration, supporting architectures and platforms developed by the company’s global teams.These technologies power products and platforms used by billions of people worldwide.Qualcomm has had a presence in India for more than 20 years, building substantial engineering capabilities across wireless, computing, artificial intelligence and system-level engineering.Qualcomm employees affected by the ongoing layoffs in India are being offered a severance package that includes two months’ notice pay, an additional month’s salary for every year of service and continued insurance cover for a year, according to employees familiar with the exit terms.The package also includes vested restricted stock units (RSUs) and those due to vest shortly, including the November tranche, along with leave encashment and the December bonus.Employees who have completed five years of service will also be eligible for gratuity. The company is providing placement assistance through a recruitment firm.
Article Summary: The job cuts come even as the US semiconductor highlighted India’s growing importance in its global engineering and semiconductor development operations. The Bengaluru campus is a key engineering hub for the development of next- generation wireless, AI, computing and system-level technologies.

Article Title: Record FPI buying in November sends sensex to near 9-month high
Article Text:
Record FPI buying in November sends sensex to near 9-month high

Investors’ wealth up by 4.3L cr

​Investors’ wealth up by 4.3L cr​

Cos’ M-cap at 510.7l cr

MUMBAI: After more than two years, foreign funds are back buying Indian stocks. In just eight trading sessions in Nov, on a net basis, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have pumped in a little over Rs 73,200 crore into Indian equities, an all-time monthly high figure that surpassed the previous record of Rs 66,135 crore in Dec 2023, data from NSDL and BSE showed.On Wednesday, FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 12,563 crore. This, combined with the recent crash in crude prices, down about 21% this month, helped Sensex gain another 1% (773 points) to close at 81,879, nearly a nine-month high level.So far in Nov, in eight trading sessions, the bellwether index has gained 10%, about 7,400 points, and investors' wealth has jumped Rs 36 lakh crore to its highest level of Rs 510.7 lakh crore, BSE data showed. During the same period, Nifty has gained 9.7% to its Wednesday close at 25,255 points. Over the last two weeks, several factors have combined to work as tailwinds for indices, market players said.For long, Indian companies were seen as laggards in the AI revolution that gripped some of the developed markets. As a result, several foreign fund managers took money off India to invest in AI-related stocks elsewhere.The trend is now reversing, benefitting the Indian market, brokers and analysts said.The recent US midterm poll results, seen as a rebuke to US President Donald Trump’s policies, raised prospects of a diplomatic solution to the war in West Asia, helping cool down crude prices and lower inflation expectations globally, including in India.As a result, the rupee strengthened and is up 1.3% this month to 93.7 to the dollar now. Relatively good corporate results for the July-Sept quarter (Q2FY27) also helped improve investor sentiment significantly.Siddhartha Khemka, head of research - wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said Indian equities are likely to retain their positive momentum, supported by an improving earnings trajectory, a sharp correction in crude prices and a strong resurgence in foreign investors’ flows.“Q2FY27 earnings are increasingly coming in ahead of expectations, strengthening confidence in corporate earnings recovery and providing fundamental support to the ongoing rally.”In Wednesday’s session, investors’ wealth went up by about Rs 4.3 lakh crore with the aggregate market value of companies listed on the BSE at Rs 510.7 lakh crore, an all-time high figure, exchange data showed.
Article Summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have pumped in a little over Rs 73,200 crore into Indian equities. Sensex gained another 1% (773 points) to close at 81,879, nearly a nine-month high level. Investors' wealth has jumped Rs 36 lakh crore to its highest level of Rs 510.7 lakh crore.

Article Title: Kolkata-Mumbai Air India flight hijack threat: Passenger apprehended after hoax note triggers security scare
Article Text:
Air India Kolkata-Mumbai flight moved to isolation bay after threat alert





KOLKATA: A passenger was apprehended and handed over to airport police in connection with a hoax hijack threat to an Air India flight from Kolkata to Mumbai, officials said on Thursday.In a release, the Airports Authority of India (AAI) said the action was taken over Wednesday’s incident involving Air India flight AI 2772, which was delayed for several hours after a handwritten threat note was found inside the aircraft’s lavatory before take-off, news agency PTI reported.The passenger was handed over to the Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International (NSCBI) Airport Police Station, it said.The note, warning that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11.10am on Wednesday, was discovered by a cabin crew member around 10.37am, prompting security agencies to initiate mandatory safety checks.All 105 passengers on board were deboarded, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for thorough security checks, PTI reported.The flight, originally scheduled to depart around 10.30am, eventually left for Mumbai at 5.38pm after authorities completed the prescribed security procedures.The threat was subsequently declared a hoax.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A passenger was apprehended and handed over to airport police in connection with a hoax hijack threat. Air India flight AI 2772 was delayed for several hours after a handwritten threat note was found inside the aircraft’s lavatory before take-off. The note, warning that the aircraft would be hijacked at 11.10am on Wednesday, was discovered by a cabin crew member.

Article Title: Thiruvananthapuram holiday on November 11: Schools and state government offices to close for Beemapally Uroos
Article Text:
Kerala holiday update: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue

Holiday applicable to schools and government offices

What is the Beemapally Uroos festival?

Beemapally Dargah's significance in Kerala

Thiruvananthapuram holiday November 11: The District Collector of Thiruvananthapuram has declared a local holiday for all educational institutions and state government offices within the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation limits on Wednesday, November 11, in connection with the annual Beemapally Uroos festival. The order applies to institutions and government offices operating within the corporation's jurisdiction.District Collector Anju K S announced the holiday as devotees prepare to participate in the annual festival at Beemapally Dargah Shareef. However, the district administration has clarified that public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to the original timetable. The holiday declaration will not affect these examinations.The local holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices situated within the boundaries of the Thiruvananthapuram Municipal Corporation. The closure has been announced specifically in view of the Beemapally Uroos celebrations.Students appearing for pre-scheduled public examinations should note that the examinations will proceed without changes.The district administration has confirmed that the existing examination schedule will remain in force despite the holiday.The declaration is limited to the specified municipal corporation area. The order does not state that the holiday applies across the entire Thiruvananthapuram district.The Beemapally Uroos, also known as the Chandanakudam Mahotsavam, is a prominent annual religious festival held at the historic Beemapally Dargah Shareef in Thiruvananthapuram. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors from different parts of Kerala and beyond.The festival commemorates the death anniversaries of Saint Sayyidhathunissa Beema Beevi and her son, Ashaikhu Sayidushaheed Maheen Aboobaker, who are buried at the shrine. According to local religious beliefs, both were descendants of the family of Prophet Muhammad.Beema Beevi and her son are remembered for their healing powers, spiritual teachings and commitment to social service. Their shrine has remained an important religious destination over several generations.Beemapally Dargah Shareef is regarded as a symbol of communal harmony in Kerala. The annual Uroos festival draws visitors from different religious communities and backgrounds, making it an important gathering in the region's religious and cultural calendar.The celebrations bring together devotees and tourists, with the shrine witnessing significant visitor participation during the 10-day festival.
Article Summary: Thiruvananthapuram declares local holiday for Beemapally Uroos, public exams to continue. The holiday covers educational institutions and state government offices. Public examinations scheduled in advance will take place according to original timetable. The 10-day celebration attracts tens of thousands of devotees, pilgrims and visitors.

Article Title: CFO Colette Kress to engineer Ian Buck - who could succeed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he exits?
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang could be ousted as per various reports

Colette Kress or Ian Buck?

External candidates and other possibilities

Nvidia's board is reportedly weighing the future of CEO Jensen Huang, turning the attention to who could take charge of the world's most valuable chipmaker if the 63-year-old executive is forced out or decides to step down.Two names have emerged as potential internal successors: Ian Buck, a veteran engineer who helped develop Nvidia's CUDA software platform, and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who has been with the company for more than a decade, reported Reuters, citing internal sources. While Buck is seen as a possible long-term choice because of his technical expertise, Kress is being viewed as a candidate who could provide continuity in the immediate term.Nvidia's board was meeting on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. Separately, reports by Bloomberg and Semafor have indicated that the board is considering an interim chief while it looks for a permanent replacement, with some board members favouring Kress for the temporary role.Huang has never named a successor. The board is also said to be working with an external firm to identify potential candidates, with possibilities ranging from senior Nvidia executives to leaders outside the company.Kress, 59, is reportedly among the most prominent internal candidates for an interim appointment. She joined Nvidia in 2013 after holding senior finance positions at Microsoft, Cisco and Texas Instruments. As CFO, she regularly appears alongside Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls, making her a familiar face to investors."Colette Kress is the obvious choice to steady the ship. She has been CFO for 13 years and fronts every earnings call alongside him, so she’s a familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst at trading platform eToro.However, the permanent leadership role could call for someone with a stronger technical background, particularly given Nvidia's position in the artificial intelligence industry. "The permanent job is a different story, though, because Nvidia’s edge comes from its technology, and the board would likely want an engineer in the chair. Someone like Ian Buck, who led the software platform that keeps developers tied to Nvidia’s chips, is the sort of internal name you’d expect to come up," Gilbert added, as quoted by Reuters.Buck, now in his late 40s, joined Nvidia in 2004 and played a key role in developing CUDA, the software platform that has helped make the company's chips central to AI development. He currently manages Nvidia's AI hardware and software products as head of product for hyperscale AI.A Stanford PhD, Buck has also been involved in Nvidia's efforts to expand its AI computing capabilities. "If a transition becomes necessary then Ian Buck is the strongest long-term internal candidate given his role in creating CUDA and leading Nvidia’s hyperscale business," said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities.The search may not be limited to Nvidia's existing leadership. Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, has also been mentioned as a possible external candidate. Jeff Fisher, a 32-year Nvidia veteran, is another name being reportedly discussed. Huang's two children, who are both executives at the company, have also mentioned in speculation about possible successors.A banker working on semiconductor deals told Reuters that Haas made the most "logical sense" because of his profile and understanding of the chip industry.Boloor also identified Haas as an external candidate worth considering. However, appointing someone from outside Nvidia could present challenges given the company's scale and the specialised nature of its business.Some investors believe the board could opt for a shared leadership arrangement, at least during the transition. "The more realistic route is an interim leader from the long-serving inner circle, possibly as a co-CEO structure: one leader to steady the business and the finances, such as Colette Kress, alongside a product and technology leader, such as Ian Buck," said Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder at Minotaur Capital, which owns Nvidia shares.The succession debate comes as Nvidia faces scrutiny over reports of two alleged extramarital relationships involving Huang. He acknowledged in a letter to employees on Sunday, admitting he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologising for violating their trust.The latest allegations include a reported relationship with Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to Huang. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at the company, reported that the relationship had not been previously disclosed. The reports have also raised questions about the company's workplace policies on conflicts of interest and personal relationships.The controversy has added to pressure on Nvidia shares. The stock lost around $430 billion in market value over Monday and Tuesday, falling a combined 9.5%. It recovered 2.9% during Wednesday's regular trading session before dropping more than 8% in after-hours trading following reports that the board was preparing to discuss Huang's future.Huang's leadership has been closely associated with the company's rise, making the prospect of a succession particularly significant for investors. "Jensen Huang is a rockstar in the industry. He’s outspoken and synonymous with the Nvidia brand, and a leader like that is very hard to replace," said Anna Wu, founder of Floodlines Research in Sydney.Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management, also pointed to the scale of Huang's contribution. "He was the one who led the marvelous rise of Nvidia," he said, adding: "I guess the question would be, can someone step up if Jensen has to resign or is forced out?"Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into the world's dominant supplier of AI processors.
Article Summary: N Nvidia's board is reportedly weighing the future of CEO Jensen Huang. Two names have emerged as potential internal successors: Ian Buck and Colette Kress. The board is also said to be working with an external firm to identify potential candidates, with possibilities ranging from senior Nvidia executives to leaders outside the company.

Article Title: 'Elon, please hire Jensen': Musk responds to X user's request on Nvidia CEO - what he said
Article Text:
Elon Musk reacts to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang controversy

Tech billionaire Elon Musk on Thursday weighed in on the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose extramarital relationship with Megaspeed International founder Alice Huang have triggered questions over possible links to Chinese intelligence.Tesla CEO Musk responded to a user on his social media platform X, who suggested that he hire Huang, writing, "Elon please hire Jensen.""That would be an honour," Musk replied.The controversy surrounding Huang has drawn attention from US lawmakers, who have raised concerns over whether his alleged relationship with a businesswoman Alice Huang suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence could have compromised American national security.Also Read| Jensen Huang had another affair with Nvidia VP who reported to him: Report Lawmakers have questioned whether China used a suspected "honeypot" scheme to influence the Nvidia CEO and whether the alleged relationship had any bearing on US decisions concerning the sale of advanced AI chips to China.Huang has acknowledged the alleged affair and reportedly discussed his infidelity with employees during meetings on Monday and Tuesday.Following his acknowledgement, Nvidia's board said it had launched an investigation into the matter.The probe is being led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.Also| As board weighs CEO Jensen Huang's 'exit', Nvidia shares fall 8% after report of second affair Separately, The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.According to the newspaper, Huang and Powell, 48, were captured on video behaving affectionately at a hotel in San Jose, California, during an Nvidia conference in March.
